chapter: Famous Door, the union dispute and Stuff Smith's last years
title: Stuff Smith the violin genius who inspired Jones and Cozy Cole
summary: On violin Stuff had perfect pitch and tireless drive; he and Cozy swung more with him than ever, and Stuff was never happier than with that group, with spontaneous head arrangements.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Fiddlers and reading violinists of New Orleans

blocks.x: Yeah, such a small thing. He could do these things like that, and then when it come to playing it was altogether a different thing. It was whole new bag then,
when he picked up the violin. He was a genius. He was a genius when he picked up his violin. Perfect pitch and all that stuff, and played more than anybody up there.

Right, never got tired. Always pushing, pushing. We both played better than we ever played in our lives, right there -- me and Cozy, because he kept pulling you "Come on. Come on. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah." You know, in his spine, you know. And I think we both swung more in those days. Maybe you know more about your horn today. You have to know more about it, technically, but I mean just down swinging it was better with him because he inspired you to do it.
I don't think he was ever as happy with anyone else, do you?

No, I think that was the best for him of all the different things he had, his trio and all of that. All that stuff never really moved him like we did. He could come down -- and all those little things we used to play with him, had no music with him. He'd get in there and think them things up himself, you know, "Crescendo (n Drums" (Singing). And he'd just be humming all that stuff to us at rehearsal, you know, and you've got to remember that night, because he's going to remember his. He's going to remember his part, sure.
